raQuotes.text: The great way of the body must be seen, as are all the archetypes of the body, to be a mirror image of the thrust of the activity of the mind. The body is the creature of the mind and is the instrument of manifestation for the fruits of mind and spirit. Therefore, you may see the body as providing the athanor through which the alchemist manifests gold.

14.jungian: Temperance is the opus: the slow, repeated work of alchemy in which material is poured back and forth until it is refined. The pouring between silver and gold cups is the circulation of energy between unconscious and conscious that gradually changes psychic material. The androgynous figure points to the union of opposites that Jung placed at the goal of individuation. Because the Great Way is always unfinished, this is sustained practice rather than a single breakthrough. This is an interpretive layer added for this app.
14.lacanian: Temperance is the unending work of symbolization: enjoyment poured through representation again and again without being exhausted. Meaning that arrives afterward, once something has been spoken or done, matches Freud's deferred action (Nachträglichkeit); this is why the Alchemist learns from manifestation and not from planning. There is no final integration, only continued working-over. This is an interpretive layer added for this app.
sources: Joseph Dartez, The Tarot According to Ra (Draft 1), pp. 118-122
Joseph Dartez, The Tarot According to Ra (Draft 1), Relationship #8, pp. 122-124
Joseph Dartez, The Tarot According to Ra (Draft 1), Note: the draft leaves the Alchemist's empowering capacity and virtues (p. 121) and its distortions (p. 122) unfinished

15.name: The Devil
15.framework: The Matrix of the Spirit is the unpotentiated spirit—the most hidden and poorly understood part of self. Here we behold the self as incomprehensible other. The spirit complex is a channel or conduit to the One Infinite Creator. The hideousness of the Adversary is inner protection against opening a link to infinite power before initiations of mind and body have taken place. The Devil is what occultists call the Dweller on the Threshold.
15.character: Dartez calls her the Adversary, and says commentators have usually misjudged her as a hedonist or a black magician to be avoided. Ra says this is the very Matrix of the spirit, the stage on which all spiritual activity plays out, so for inner work she is to be sought out. She is feminine, so she is known from the outside: the Adversary is the inner experience of realizing that someone else sees us as the Devil. She is deeply misunderstood and often amused by the hatred; what others hate is her refusal of their rules for right and wrong, and she feels no remorse because to her the acts are not wrong. She is neither positive nor negative: she follows the idea that if it feels right it is right, so she is capricious, lascivious but honest, or generous but cruel, and she enjoys the strength of feeling in an act whatever its moral direction, especially when it is forbidden. Her function is to guard the channel to the Creator against use before the mind and body have been initiated; her ugliness is the inner protection, and the Dweller on the Threshold of the occultists. Once initiations are done she becomes less ugly. Her empowering capacity is authenticity and her virtue is the courage to face vitriol for what she represents. Dartez also frames this archetype in a larger setting: Ra's description of the Matrix and Potentiator of the Spirit is of the One Original Thought, not of our own Archetypal Mind, and spirit's movements come in sudden moments and lingering feelings, not as continuous daily change.
symbols: Typhon, centre of the card - a composite of crocodile head (violence and cruelty), bat wings (night; Ra's 'primeval darkness'), pig's body and tail (revelry in filth), snake from the navel (gluttony, and a blockage of the higher energy centers), erect penis (the same blockage and unquenchable desire; Ra confirms this reading at 84.19), a scepter in the right hand and a torch pointing down in the left (a source of light wasted, spiritual power misused)
Breasts and penis together - Dartez rejects the older reading that this shows an inability to love and offers instead sterility: the inability to generate or be fruitful

Two broken pillars underfoot - the pillars of the Significator of the Mind, not of the Potentiator: our own conceptual separation of good from evil, which we shelter behind as in a storm; Typhon tramples it, leaving rubble and vulnerability

Two kneeling figures chained at the neck, in goat's-head masks - the conscious and unconscious selves, also self and other, captive to each other; the masks show they follow social norms without thinking, which puts them in Typhon's service; they point in opposite directions, so they want to go opposite ways and neither can move

The figures also stand for three things at once - being locked in a prison with a servant of the Devil, being a spiritual slave to society's rules, and the army of Typhon's followers who say contradictory things because they are seized by the Devil

levels.personal: The Shadow, Jung's rejected self. Our most hated traits sit together in the dark of the unconscious, fed by their link to who we are as expressions of the Creator, so they are hidden sources of power. We are afraid of what we might do without the shackles of social norms, and sometimes act out exactly what we hate and enjoy it because we think it wrong. We end up prisoners shackled to what we hate.
levels.interpersonal: The Rival: the kind of person we hate most, a mirror we resemble while trying to be their opposite. We cannot be indifferent to them. When we are the Rival to someone else, we feel the attraction without the hatred and laugh at the attacks because they rest on a morality we have rejected. Ra says marriages are often 'adversary relationships' (31.16); Dartez reads that as the partner reflecting our unconscious back to us, so we see our own Shadow in them.
levels.social: The Enemy. She is not an iconoclast who defines herself against the norms; she does as she likes and the prevailing norms single her out. Social life divides into two camps because each group builds its Enemy as the inversion of its own worldview.

polarizedExpressions.note: Like all Matrices, the Matrix of the Spirit has no polarized expression. Dartez says the Adversary is neither positively nor negatively oriented.

distortions: The Adversary in the closet - she lives her controversial truth but hides it to avoid backlash, so she is shielded from others and potentiation never happens
The ostentatious Devil - she plays the Devil so loudly and trolls so much that it shuts down any chance of potentiation, and endangers her as an incarnate creature

raQuotes.text: The Matrix of the Spirit is what you may call the Night of the Soul, or Primeval Darkness. Again we have that which is not capable of movement or work.
Therefore, the melody, shall we say, of this Matrix often seems to be of a negative and evil, as you would call it, nature.

In this context you may see the one you call Lucifer as the true light-bringer in that the knowledge of good and evil both precipitated the mind/body/spirits of this Logos from the Edenic conditions of constant contentment but also provided the impetus to move, to work, and to learn.
The adept, whether positive or negative, has the same Matrix. The Potentiator is also identical.

15.jungian: The Devil is the Shadow in the full Jungian sense: what the ego has rejected, still linked to the Self and therefore potent. Chained figures in goat masks suggest a persona-ego pair held together by collective values nobody has examined. The 'Dweller on the Threshold' idea corresponds to the guardian every initiation has to pass, and the ugliness of the figure is proportional to how long it has been rejected. This is an interpretive layer added for this app.
15.lacanian: The Devil is the Other as the place of forbidden enjoyment: what the symbolic order marks as prohibited becomes the site of the greatest pull. The two chained figures are the divided subject, each treating the other as the enemy, joined by the prohibition itself. Her feeling no remorse points to desire that has not been captured by the guilt structure of the law. The 'Enemy' at the social level is a familiar function: a group needs an external figure to hold what it cannot own. This is an interpretive layer added for this app.
sources: Joseph Dartez, The Tarot According to Ra (Draft 1), pp. 124-128
Joseph Dartez, The Tarot According to Ra (Draft 1), Ra, 84.19 (cited by Dartez for the erect-penis symbol)

16.name: Lightning Struck Tower
16.framework: The Potentiator of the Spirit represents sudden spiritual awakening. The pyramid/tower is the place of initiation—the temple constructed by human hands, the mental construct designed to secure favorable character arc in our life narrative. Lightning destroys the pinnacle of holiness in which we've made ourselves cozy, knocking both transparent and hidden self out of the temple, crashing to the ground in abject humiliation.
16.character: Dartez calls him the Disgraced Priest. He is masculine, so he is active, but we do not choose when awakening arrives; what we do choose is the tower. We build a lightning rod by deciding that we are already enlightened, already good, already well polarized, which we manage by splitting the spirit and burying the Devil deep, then sitting at the top and looking down on everyone else. An event then shows us how wrong we were about how close to the Creator we are; the event itself is not the point, the illumination is. Our whole story about ourselves fails; the rejected self, symbolized by the woman falling from the tower, is exposed too. He is the personification of hypocrisy and spiritual embarrassment: his standards were built to hide his vices, and his inner circle turns against him. In Relationship #9 ('Revelation') the Devil and the Priest are chained together as Jekyll and Hyde, which is the Dark Night of the Soul; when the revelation comes, the two falling figures are no longer chained. It is painful but liberating, because the belief system that split the mind is gone and the conscious and unconscious can start over as partners.
symbols: Tower or pyramid - not the spirit but the temple in which we try to use spirit to contact the Creator (the traditional 'House of God'); built entirely by human hands, like the temple of the Storyteller in the Significator of the Mind; Dartez reads it as the mental construct of beliefs we built to get closer to the Creator, which hardened into dogma, and not as material achievement
Capstone or crown dislodged - the pinnacle of holiness or moral rectitude where the transparent spiritual self settled; almost everyone places themselves at the top of their own ideology
Lightning - sudden spiritual awakening; Dartez notes the Sun as its source, which fits because the Potentiator is the inner Logos, so we do not choose when it comes

Two figures falling - in the Egyptian deck both are male, one crowned and one not, usually read as awakening striking anyone regardless of rank; Dartez prefers the male-female version because it connects the card to the Devil before it and the Sun after it: the transparent and hidden selves are in this together

Losing the 'penthouse' - the collapse can be wholly inward, a discovery that we were less advanced than we thought, or an actual loss of status; what matters is the spiritual and moral value of the self-image

levels.personal: A truth about ourselves comes clearly into view despite our efforts to hide it. Dartez argues lying to oneself is a relationship between the conscious self and the witness about the nature of the unconscious: the conscious self keeps building more elaborate explanations to quiet the witness, until the truth comes out in a way it cannot deny.
levels.interpersonal: Usually an explosive encounter with our Rival: a public quarrel with a lover, a workplace clash that penalizes both, a social media fight. It need not be a conflict; a spark of attraction to a forbidden partner, or a conversation with someone we are inclined to dislike, can be enough to collapse our self-conception.
levels.social: The literal Disgraced Priest: a sudden turn of events that reveals a secret affinity with the forbidden. A scandal for witnesses, earth-shattering for the person.

polarizedExpressions.note: Like all Potentiators, this archetype has no polarized expression. The draft's heading for polarized expressions and distortions in this chapter is left empty.

raQuotes.text: The potential power of this extremely receptive Matrix is such that the Potentiator may be seen as Lightning. In your archetypical system called the tarot this has been refined into the concept complex of the Lightning Struck Tower. However, the original Potentiator was light in its sudden and fiery form; that is, the lightning itself.
Thusly one may see the Matrix as the deepest darkness and the Potentiator of Spirit as the most sudden awakening, illuminating, and generative influence.

16.jungian: The Tower is the collapse of an inflated persona. Having identified with the 'enlightened' pole, the ego has pushed the Shadow down until the pressure produces an eruption. Jung would call the fall a necessary deflation: the move from ego-centered spirituality toward the Self. The unchained falling figures match the idea that the conscious and unconscious can relate as partners once the split between them has been given up. This is an interpretive layer added for this app.
16.lacanian: The Tower is the collapse of an ego-ideal. The 'smug satisfaction' of the Priest is the position of the subject presumed to be good, and the lightning is the Real breaking through the story that held it off. Hypocrisy here is structural: the standards exist to cover the very enjoyment they forbid. What changes after the fall is not that the subject learns a new fact but that the fantasy that sustained its position no longer works. This is an interpretive layer added for this app.
sources: Joseph Dartez, The Tarot According to Ra (Draft 1), pp. 128-131
Joseph Dartez, The Tarot According to Ra (Draft 1), Relationship #9, pp. 131-134

17.name: The Star
17.framework: The Catalyst of the Spirit depicts the unconscious mind fully exposed after the Revelation of the Potentiator. The lodestar is the Logos shining through the dark night of the spirit complex. The seven smaller stars represent energy centers through which the Logos expresses itself—they must be open, unblocked, and minimally balanced so spiritual work may be done. The two triangles show right and left-hand paths as mirror images within the lodestar.
17.character: Dartez calls her the Faithful. Ra says he prefers the name Faith to Hope (80.13). Faith is not belief without evidence, since belief is mental. It is trust: on the right-hand path, trust in the sincere benevolence of the universe, the Creator and other people, with attention fixed on the light and no checking for proof, since looking for evidence of having chosen well would be faithless. After the lightning she is exposed and vulnerable, no longer able or willing to defend herself, grateful the caged life as a demon is over. The star shows her destiny but with two faces: a glorious unfolding of the higher will, and the shadow of an empty universe with no Creator. So she has doubts, and Dartez says to be the Faithful is to live through despair, which is a mixture of positive and negative faith. Her faith is a necessary absurdity: achieving the ideal is hopeless, yet she cannot live without faith in the eventual manifestation of the hopeless. The spirit's domain is aesthetic: we pick a path not because it is right but because one side of the star strikes us as more beautiful. The draft gives this archetype no empowering capacity or virtues.
symbols: Naked woman kneeling, facing her own left - the unconscious mind, fully exposed after the Revelation; her desires and values are visible but not why she feels or follows the star as she does, so the mystery of her link to the star is magnified

Lodestar - the Logos shining through the dark night of the spirit complex into her awareness; the seven smaller stars around it are the energy centers or 'seals', which must be open and minimally balanced for spiritual work

Two triangles in the star (white above an inverted black) - the paths are mirror images, with the left-hand path the shadow or illusory image of the right; both are in view whenever we face the Logos in faith, and the opposite path dims as we progress but never disappears

Pitchers pouring onto land and sea - unlike the Alchemist, who refines energies without adding or removing any, the Faithful lets spiritual energy pass through her and out into the world without looking back; it enters from the star through her eyes and leaves through her hands; the outpouring is also the shedding of the norms that caged her

Flower with a butterfly - spring after devastation; the fertile ground of acts of faith on the right-hand path (the left-hand path is an endless void that swallows everything with no thanks); the butterfly is the acquisition of wings, which is how the inner witness crosses the dark gap between the earthbound mind and the Logos
Night sky - the veiled spirit complex; Ra says the shadow of hidden things holds the power of the Creator (80.8)
Legs at right angles - the draft says this shows how close the physical and metaphysical are, then adds in a note to itself, 'but what does this really mean??'; it is unresolved there

levels.personal: The inner motivation to act on a deep sense of rightness, not on a rule or on moral goodness. When we are present to that 'resonance' we feel impelled to act regardless of what the world thinks, and want to be a conduit for the energy that has opened; our inner state stays hidden from the world, and we want it to fill the world.
levels.interpersonal: A relationship that has just been through Revelation. The mental structures that kept it static, with the Priest separated from the Demon, are gone, so we approach rebuilding it naively, hopeful and fearful together. What was offensive may now look attractive, and our partner's changed view of us lets us relax and be natural without fear of being demonized for it.
levels.social: The formerly rejected element of a group, after an earth-shattering event changes the group's rules. We feel liberated and daunted: pressure to be more than we feel we are, plus a worry the new hope is unfounded.

polarizedExpressions.rightHandPath: Wholesome through and through. Having endured deep suffering she comes out pure of heart: the parts that seemed vicious are revealed as youthful, pristine and longing for a loving world, the unconscious mind reborn as an angelic state, living in service to the Creator she sees.
polarizedExpressions.leftHandPath: The Broken Soul. The human will is finally broken; she has seen through the universe and found no savior, no benevolence and no escape from isolation. With no refuge, she loses the will to fight, hollows herself out to match the loveless centre of the spirit, and offers herself as a vessel for her oppressor, the conscious mind, to use as it likes. Most people are somewhere between these poles, and the pull between trusting the hidden self and wanting it gone (an innocent child that wants out of the cage, and a pest that will not behave) is what produces despair. Dartez says despair is the doom of human spiritual striving: few escape it, and faith only requires honesty about what we see in the star.

raQuotes.text: This archetype is the Catalyst of the Spirit and, because of the illuminations of the Potentiator of the Spirit, will begin to cause these changes in the adept's viewpoint.
The shadow of hidden things is an infinite depth in which is stored the power of the One Infinite Creator.

17.jungian: The Star is the first calm after the Tower: the ego has given up its defenses and is receptive to the Self, shown as the lodestar. The pouring out is closer to a surrender of ego-control than to an act. The two triangles are the opposites held in the Self, and the despair Dartez describes matches the tension of holding them without resolving it. The flower and butterfly are classic symbols of renewal and the soul. This is an interpretive layer added for this app.
17.lacanian: The Star marks the subject after the fantasy has dropped: no longer defended, it faces the question of what the Other wants of it, a question the star poses without answering. Faith as 'a necessary absurdity' resembles desire's relation to an object that cannot be reached. The two outcomes, a Creator who gives meaning or a void that takes everything, are the two ways the subject can answer: as instrument of a larger will, or as its own master and a hollowed-out servant of it. This is an interpretive layer added for this app.
sources: Joseph Dartez, The Tarot According to Ra (Draft 1), pp. 134-139
Joseph Dartez, The Tarot According to Ra (Draft 1), Ra, 80.13 (the name Faith) and 80.8

18.name: The Moon
18.framework: The Experience of the Spirit shows the environment through which spiritual catalyst moves. The two pyramids are temples of spiritual initiation—one white (right-hand path, with door) and one black (left-hand path, no door). The Moon offers dim light but is not fixed like a star—it cannot offer an objective marker. The night sky and environment are filled with shadows, illusions, potential guides and hidden threats. There is no human figure because we leave the mind behind; no reasoning helps here.
18.character: Dartez calls him the Watcher in the Night. He guards the path along which the Catalyst of the Spirit moves, staying outside the temple to ward off two kinds of spirit: those who would lure the Faithful to the opposite of what they wanted, and those who would destroy and feed on them. He senses polarities and intentions by something like smell (as the jackal and scorpion do), not by sight. He never enters the temple of initiation; he is the bodhisattva who vows not to finish his own journey until everyone else has finished theirs, and the price of his vigilance is that he cannot look at the pure light as the Faithful does. On the right-hand path he is a worrier and protector, the Guardian of the Temple, like a father protecting his daughter, who lives exposed to darkness so others do not have to. On the left-hand path he is a con-artist in his element, the Pied Piper. Both are described in more detail in Relationship #10 ('Entourage'): the Guardian takes the Faithful by the arm and walks her forward, as peers in different roles, while the Pied Piper takes a desperate Broken Soul and turns her into a servant. The draft gives no empowering capacity or virtues for him. The card has no human figure, so there is no obvious point of view; the Traveler can be imagined as riding the butterfly from the ground toward the star.
symbols: White pyramid (left, with a door) and black pyramid (right, no door) - the two temples of initiation, each a new mental configuration for spiritual work that will become the next dogma (the next Matrix of the Spirit) as well as a release from the previous one; the doorway shows the right-hand path is easier to enter, and the black pyramid has to be cut into

Moon behind cloud or mist - a dim, diffuse reflection of the Logos; unlike a star it is not fixed, so it gives no objective bearing; the night itself holds shadows, illusions, guides and threats (Ra links moonlight to chimera and falsity, 80.8)
No human figure - we leave the mind behind, since reasoning is no help here; what is transparent to us is only that we are Travelers in a strange and frightening world

Scorpion in a circle of light, crawling toward the black jackal and white pyramid - a small, nocturnal, deadly hunter that tracks by smell; the spiritual predator that feeds on the unsuspecting; it aims at the right-hand path, where prey is easier

Two jackals facing each other (black left, white right) - nocturnal scavengers associated with the dead; each guards its own pyramid; the white one looks sleek and trustworthy and leads the naive right-hand seeker to servitude at the wrong temple; the black one is drab and plain and helps whoever asks, though few find it

levels.personal: Often subsumed into the superego. The inner Watcher is our awareness of the dangers on the little-trodden path of faith, which social norms mark taboo for a reason, and our sense of responsibility for bringing the fragile, trusting part of ourselves through to its intended spiritual experience.
levels.interpersonal: A protector, a shield between the vulnerable and predators; the traditional father's role. He does not try to make his partner less naive, but preserves her by hardening himself.
levels.social: The Warrior, notably in policing. This shows the morally mixed nature of the persona: the police try to be a shield against the dangers of the night and also act as predators on the vulnerable under cover of protection.

polarizedExpressions.rightHandPath: The Guardian: a selfless protector entirely oriented to the wellbeing of those he protects. He seeks no awards, status, wealth or praise, appears as the black jackal, humble and unremarkable, with a hidden radiance. He does not fight fire with fire; as Ra says, love is the great protector (63.5), and he builds a loving support system like a chain of people holding hands along the path. He fights only when necessary and would give his life rather than harm those he protects. Mixed form (attempting to polarize positive): he believes his own lie that he is a selfless guardian, mistakes the vulnerable for threats, harms them, demands respect and accolades, and his acclaim becomes a way to silence critics, so that with the best of intentions he enslaves others.
polarizedExpressions.leftHandPath: The Pied Piper: a predator so subtle his victims never know. He is attractive, with health, wealth, status and fame, projects a shameless false image as a Guardian, draws in vulnerable seekers who want a protective leader, sets up an unequal energy exchange, and builds a conceptual cage so they feel there is no escape. The black pyramid has no door because left-hand initiation is impossible for the follower (she remains a servant) and escape from the Pied Piper is impossible. Mixed form (attempting to polarize negative): he lacks the toughness and self-esteem to carry the scam off, shows insecurity when he is not praised, stays attached to his glossy image, and makes too many enemies, which breaks the spell.

distortions: The scorpion: the Watcher who has lost his sanity through exposure to the illusions of the night, to whom everything is a threat; there are no vulnerable people, only predators, so he is permanently on guard and ready to strike anyone who moves too quickly; Dartez says the mixed positive Watcher is attuned to scorpions because that is how he pictures his enemies

raQuotes.text: The Experience of the Spirit, that which you have called the Moon, is then, by far, the more manifest of influences upon the polarity of the adept.

Even the most unhappy of experiences, shall we say, which seem to occur in the catalyst of the adept, seen from the viewpoint of the spirit, may, with the discrimination possible in shadow, be worked with until light equaling the light of brightest noon descends upon the adept and positive or service-to-others illumination has occurred.

You may, with some fruitfulness, consider the possibilities of moonlight. You are aware that we have described the Matrix of the Spirit as a night. The moonlight, then, offers either a true picture seen in shadow, or chimera and falsity.

18.jungian: The Moon is the realm of the unconscious as the dim light of intuition, which can reveal or deceive. The Watcher is a figure of the superego or protective persona that the psyche posts at the threshold of the unknown, and Dartez's own personal-level reading says so. The two temples and two jackals image the same fork Jung saw in any contact with the numinous: toward integration or toward inflation and possession by the archetype. The Pied Piper is what an inflated ego does with the energy of the Self. This is an interpretive layer added for this app.
18.lacanian: The Moon is the field of the imaginary at its most deceptive: the dim light that gives images with no fixed point. The jackals are two ways the Other can present itself, the attractive one that captures and the plain one that serves. The Pied Piper is a figure of the master who makes himself the one who 'knows,' building a follower's dependency on his supposed knowledge. The scorpion is paranoia: the fear that everything is out to destroy one. This is an interpretive layer added for this app.
sources: Joseph Dartez, The Tarot According to Ra (Draft 1), pp. 139-142
Joseph Dartez, The Tarot According to Ra (Draft 1), Relationship #10, pp. 142-145
Joseph Dartez, The Tarot According to Ra (Draft 1), Ra, 63.5 and 80.8

19.name: The Sun
19.framework: The Significator of the Spirit is 'that living entity which either radiates or absorbs the love and light of the One Infinite Creator, radiates it to others or absorbs it for the self.' The image shows the masculine and feminine spiritual selves joining hands in a sunlit setting—having a picnic. As Ra says, some enjoy the sun beautiful, food delicious, games refreshing; others find the night delicious, their picnic being pain and the examination of perversities.
19.character: Dartez calls him the Celebrant, the self that is a living party. The word is meant broadly: any gathering oriented toward pleasure together. Parties have a vibe, and the vibe decides what happens when someone's inner demon is exposed: with a loving, supportive group the exposure brings people closer, while in other groups it invites exploitation. The Celebrant is that vibe, not a task-doer; there is nothing he needs to accomplish. He is here 'to boogie,' fully in the present, and people come because of who he is. For him pleasure and contact with the divine overlap: the sacred always takes the shape of the pleasant. His vibe is not necessarily polarized in either direction; a pure polarity is hard-won through transformation, and the Celebrant cannot change his vibe, only live it. Dartez points out that this card is the most misunderstood in the deck. Commentators assumed a single, right-hand path and read the happiness as success on it, and Ra's description, which Dartez cites (80.17), shows two options instead. He also notes Ra says very little about this image. In Relationship #11 ('Company') the Traveler lodges with the Celebrant and takes on his vibe; eventually she sees the conflict between his two kinds of delight, pities him, and leaves.
symbols: Man and woman holding hands, face to face, in a circle of flowers - the same figures as Arcana 4 (bird on the chest) and 2 (ankh on the chest), but Dartez reads them as the transparent and hidden sides of the spirit and not of the mind: the bird in flight is the inner witness flying from the earth to union with the Creator, and the ankh is the power of the infinite passing through the veiled incarnate experience into manifestation and back

Circle of flowers - a spiritual circle marking sacred from mundane space; they stay inside it, so for the spirit all of life takes place in sacred space; made of flowers for natural beauty, fecundity and grace
Sun with a lingam-yoni inside - the Logos, shining regardless of path; the ongoing spiritual experience as continuous ecstatic union of masculine and feminine

Picnic and 'to boogie' - Dartez reads the scene as a picnic and cites Ra's picnic passage (19.17), which treats love of light and love of darkness as equal forms of play, so the card is not just the right-hand path

Holding hands and gazing into each other's eyes - exaltation of the other above oneself, so it can be read both ways: on the right-hand path the masculine helps the feminine along toward the vision she chooses and exalts her; on the left, the feminine gives up her light for the masculine's purposes
Youthful, lightly clothed figures - described, with no meaning given

levels.personal: Our personal vibe: the integration of the Creator's light as it passes through our own Catalyst and Experience of the Spirit. How we handle our inner demons and their exposure gives each of us a signature, and our moral quality shows to others who feel it.
levels.interpersonal: Welcoming someone into our spiritual state, often when they visit our home. How we speak and touch, treat small animals and decorate our space shows how we take pleasure in morally significant things, usually in a morally mixed way.
levels.social: The representative of a group who attracts or repels others just by being a good or bad energetic fit with them: not through action, belief or shared values, but by showing them a good time. It shows up in performance and spectator sports, where soulful versus soulless music is the difference.

polarizedExpressions.rightHandPath: The Unicorn. Being near the Unicorn makes others feel more like themselves, because their thorough self-acceptance and radiance of the Creator's light is contagious. Only those committed to the left-hand path, who find such self-acceptance disgusting, are repelled.
polarizedExpressions.leftHandPath: The Vampire (Succubus, Incubus, Harpy). Polished, exactly who they mean to be, as alluring as they are terrifying. People feel the pull, release their own vibe and enter the Vampire's, and find pleasure in the harm of others or of themselves, so victims give themselves willingly. The mixed form (the usual one, either direction) is the False Guru at the centre of a cult of personality: uplifting and exploiting by turns, love-bombing one day and shaming the next.

distortions: Misery - the Celebrant who indulges in spiritual displeasure or joylessness ('misery loves company') and draws in people who match that vibe; Dartez labels this 'mixed (or distorted?)' and notes the card is usually read as joy, which fits only the right-hand version

raQuotes.text: The Significator of the Spirit is that living entity which either radiates or absorbs the love and the light of the One Infinite Creator: radiates it to others or absorbs it for the self.
Some love the light. Some love the darkness. It is a matter of the unique and infinitely various Creator choosing and playing among its experiences as a child upon a picnic.

19.jungian: The Sun here is the Self radiating through a person who has taken in the Shadow. Dartez's insistence that the vibe cannot be faked fits Jung's view that personality is felt more than argued. The union of masculine and feminine, the conjunctio, is the central image; his twist is that it can be lived in either moral direction, and that the False Guru is the inflated persona that fascinates others. This is an interpretive layer added for this app.
19.lacanian: The Sun is enjoyment that has found a form: the sacred identified through the pleasant, where the draft's identification of the divine with pleasure comes close to what Lacan calls jouissance. Whether it is ethical depends on whether the circuit is open (the Unicorn lets others be more themselves) or closed (the Vampire uses the other as a supply). The False Guru is the subject supposed to know, who holds followers by alternating affirmation and shaming. This is an interpretive layer added for this app.
sources: Joseph Dartez, The Tarot According to Ra (Draft 1), pp. 145-150
Joseph Dartez, The Tarot According to Ra (Draft 1), Relationship #11, pp. 150-152
Joseph Dartez, The Tarot According to Ra (Draft 1), Ra, 80.17 and 19.17 (both cited by Dartez)

20.name: Awakening
20.framework: The Transformation of the Spirit depicts spiritual rebirth. Three figures emerge from a sarcophagus—male, female, and child (the unified spirit into which gendered sides transform when they merge). They are bound and unable to move, indicating that in this energy there is nothing to be done except stop struggling and allow the process to occur. The sarcophagus represents the physical illusion's limitations. Emerging does not mean leaving limitations behind—the spirit no longer feels trapped within them.
20.character: Dartez calls her the Prophet, named for the isolation and torment of the biblical prophets, who are rarely honored in their lifetimes. The card shows the result, but the stage before matters as much: a living death in which, to the spirit, we feel already entombed. Nothing excites or pleases, no emotions stir, there is little desire to do anything, and the will to live is sapped; Dartez says this can look like clinical depression, but means it only when there is no neurological or hormonal cause. The tomb is the physical world and its limits: the body, the incarnation, the obligations that cannot be removed. The call can only be heard in this state, because creature comforts would drown it out. After the call comes rejection: it asks for a complete realignment of how we take pleasure, which invites social scorn, and the Prophet often feels unequal to it, as the biblical prophets did. The only real choice is to accept the call or stay in the tomb, which is the middle way. Heeding the call is simply continuing to listen. The masculine figure emerges first because the transparent side of spirit is the one most likely to resist, by shutting the call out or trying to bring back old pleasures. In Relationship #12 ('Salvation') the Prophet meets the Avatar, whose joy is a signal strong enough to resonate through the walls of the tomb. The draft gives no empowering capacity or virtues for the Prophet.
symbols: Male, female and child figures rising from a sarcophagus, wrapped in burial cloth - the veiled and transparent sides of the self and their offspring, the unified spirit that comes from their union; they are bound and cannot move, so there is nothing to do but stop struggling and let it happen
Rectangular sarcophagus - the physical illusion, a state of limitation; emerging is not leaving the limits behind (the body stays a body) but the spirit not feeling trapped in them

Winged trumpeter with a tongue of fire, sounding toward the lower right - the Creator reaching into the spirit complex; the trumpet aims right because only the right-hand path hears a call from beyond; on the left, we must call ourselves
Rays of light - illumination of the new world with meaning and purpose

Square banner with a cross (on older versions) - the square is the physical illusion and the cross the necessity of sacrifice: right, left, or carry on, and choosing one rejects the others; Dartez notes that at this stage the real options are only to polarize further or stay entombed

Scarab beetle on the sarcophagus - the dung beetle lays eggs in its dung so the young hatch surrounded by food; renewal and resurrection, and the repeated nature of the Transformation: it happens over and over

levels.personal: Coming to terms with what cannot change: a disability, a financial barrier, an unrealizable dream, a permanent loss. We may keep praying for the miracle, but the work is learning to love life amid the limit, living joyously through it and not despite it. The inner Prophet has to give up dependence on hoping for the hopeless, which was what faith in the Catalyst depended on and is now an obstacle. Rebirth shows up as new sources of joy and purpose.
levels.interpersonal: A crisis point in a relationship in which each person plays one side: both can no longer enjoy it, both feel captive, and one is holding it back in the tomb while the other is stuck under their weight. Common in loveless but enduring marriages, where the problem is boredom and not hatred. The way out is usually not outward separation but a change in openness to pleasure, after which the relationship (the child) is born into something new.
levels.social: An organization that was once enthusiastic and indulgent in its work now plods through the usual steps, with no zest, everyone wishing the ordeal were over although all depend on it.

polarizedExpressions.rightHandPath: The Prophet awaits a call from beyond the personal incarnate self. The inner witness always sees from the incarnate perspective, and even mystical unity is felt as losing oneself in something larger; that Creator beyond the self is where the call comes from. Having found that his own efforts are marred by mixed motives, he admits powerlessness, in the spirit of the first steps of a twelve-step program, and trusts the Creator completely. When he does, the call sounds, the tomb opens and a higher will gives him new ways to enjoy life. Dartez's motto for this path: when life hands you lemons, learn to love lemons.
polarizedExpressions.leftHandPath: For the left-hand Prophet nothing exists beyond the incarnate self. His entombment is a festering of the wounds others have inflicted through his weaknesses, a lump of anger and self-loathing. It ends when something in him must die, and his own will to crush his weakness and manifest more power than his rivals calls him out: the mummified man tearing through the wrappings and smashing his way out. Dartez remarks that our culture often celebrates this as a heroic virtue without seeing it as a left-hand ideal.

raQuotes.text: That which you call the sarcophagus in your system may be seen to be the material world, if you will. This material world is transformed by the spirit into that which is infinite and eternal.

The infinity of the spirit is an even greater realization than the infinity of consciousness, for consciousness which has been disciplined by will and faith is that consciousness which may contact intelligent infinity directly.

20.jungian: Awakening is the death-rebirth pattern at the level of the Self: the ego is bound and passive, and what comes is a call from a source beyond it. The three figures, the pair and the child, suggest the coniunctio and its fruit. The living-death stage resembles the 'dark night' that precedes a change of attitude. The left-hand version, in which the ego calls itself out, looks like an inflation, an ego that does not recognize anything greater than itself. This is an interpretive layer added for this app.
20.lacanian: Awakening is a drive-level standstill: desire has gone quiet, and the way out is not an act of the subject but a call from the Other (a 'vocation' in the old sense of being called). The right-hand Prophet gives up the fantasy of mastery and accepts being addressed; the left-hand Prophet tries to be his own Other, and so must supply the call himself, which is the difficulty Dartez points out. Learning to love the limit is, in these terms, a change in how one relates to the unchangeable real. This is an interpretive layer added for this app.
sources: Joseph Dartez, The Tarot According to Ra (Draft 1), pp. 152-157
Joseph Dartez, The Tarot According to Ra (Draft 1), Relationship #12, pp. 161-164
Joseph Dartez, The Tarot According to Ra (Draft 1), Note: the draft has no distortions for this archetype; the section ends with an exercise on identifying the "tomb" and "lemons" in your own life

21.name: The World
21.framework: The Great Way of the Spirit shows the ultimate union—the successful completion of the Great Work of third density. The lingam-yoni with wings surrounded by a circle of flowers represents commitment to a single moral polarity pure and enduring enough to traverse the strait and narrow path to union with Creator. The circle of flowers is no longer on ground but in sky—the sacred circle is now mobile, surrounding the union wherever it flies. As Ra says, daily activity becomes 'sacramental.'
21.character: Dartez calls the persona the Avatar, borrowing the idea of religious figures such as Jesus, Buddha and Krishna who were both human and the divine. This is an aspirational Great Way persona: we get closer to the ideal by trusting it is already realized in us, 'the crown is already upon the head' (Dartez quotes this phrase; in Ra it appears at 49.6 about the north pole of the energy centers, not about this archetype). The Avatar lives in the constant flow of the Creator's energy into manifestation, neither doubts the connection nor hesitates to act out whatever is called for, and exists in a bliss that comes from the ever-changing union of masculine and feminine in the spirit. We do not have to match Jesus or Buddha to become it, but mind and body must be initiated and we must have done real work on our own demons. It often wakes during a mystical experience, which is a Transformation of the Spirit, and from then on a slow-burning desire to live that union all our days takes hold. The Avatar's strength is not perfection but total commitment to the rhythm of Transformations washing over the incarnate self, wave after wave; they refuse to look away from the movements of the spirit, positive or negative, and trust the Creator is at the center of every experience. The draft gives no empowering capacity or virtues. In Relationship #12 the Avatar is a messenger whose joy resonates through a Prophet's tomb.
symbols: Kneeling woman in white, playing a three-stringed harp - the feminine side of the spirit playing the masculine as an instrument; the masculine freely hands the reins of spiritual growth to the hidden side, where the power is locked; music shows the power does not come through intellect, physical discipline or ritual but through feeling, rhythm and flow; the strings are mind, body and spirit, all given over to her
Crowned man's head on the harp - found in the Zain and Fatham images but not in Falconnier-Wegener or Saint Germain; Dartez prefers it but admits it may not be original

Winged lingam-yoni above - the union of the primal masculine and feminine, the transparent self entering the hidden self and fertilizing darkness with light (in the spirit, Matrix and Potentiator); not to be read literally as sex; it means the Great Work of third density is complete in the sense of commitment to a single, pure and lasting polarity, and the wings mean we can fly up to the Sun

Circle of flowers, now in the sky around the lingam-yoni - the sacred circle is now mobile; it goes wherever the union goes, so daily life becomes sacramental (49.6) and all of Creation is holy ground

Heads of the four sphinx creatures (human, lion, bull, eagle) around the wreath - mentioned as a new element, not interpreted in this chapter; compare the magician's four virtues on the Catalyst of the Body

Compared with the Sun card - the Sun is gone, replaced by the winged lingam-yoni, the flowers have moved from the ground to the sky, and the feminine now has the power, plucking the masculine, where they were equal before

levels.personal: Stepping toward the ideal by trusting it is already ours, and living in the constant flow of the Creator's energy into manifestation without looking away from the spirit's movements, joyful or painful.
levels.interpersonal: One person gives themselves over, body and soul, to the other without hesitation or fear, trusting that she knows best how to use his abilities; she depends on him to link her to the manifest world, since without him she is 'full of music that she cannot play.' Dartez suggests the guru-chela relationship and, for those who spurn gurus, sexual intercourse as the easiest place to experience it.
levels.social: Constructive anarchist organization: the group itself knows best what is best for it, and each member serves as an instrument of its higher intentions. Dartez notes this can easily be perverted into cultism.

polarizedExpressions.rightHandPath: The masculine self submits to the higher will embodied in the feminine, trusting her fully as the hand of the Creator, offering himself as her servant, confident a more harmonious world will result. She, an embodiment of infinite love, is honored by the trust and works to fulfil his deepest desires better than he could imagine.
polarizedExpressions.leftHandPath: Dartez says he has never experienced this side, and bases it on what left-hand adepts say and on his own sense of what the opposite must be. The adept uses the Lesser Cycle to empty the Shadow (the feminine side) and reorient it to the conscious self's intent, which Dartez compares to brainwashing by illusion, punishment and reward. The incarnate self wants power, dominion and glorification as a god. Once the Shadow is judged tamed, it is released into the world: he mounts her like a dragon, and despite her far greater power she acts out his wishes. Her power flows through him as a musician through an instrument, but it is his will that is carried out. Dartez says the jealous gods of religion are expressions of this adept.

raQuotes.text: One may also see the reflection of this contact (as well) as the contact with intelligent energy, which is the universe, or, as you have called it somewhat provincially, the world.
The contact with intelligent infinity is most likely to produce an unspeakable joy in the entity experiencing such contact.

21.jungian: The World is the endpoint of individuation described as service to a larger order: the ego puts itself at the Self's disposal. The flying lingam-yoni is the coniunctio in motion, and the mobile circle of flowers is a sacred space no longer tied to a place. Dartez's left-hand version, taming the Shadow and riding it, is what Jung would call inflation: the ego appropriating the Self's energy for itself. This is an interpretive layer added for this app.
21.lacanian: The Great Way of the Spirit is the position of being an instrument of the Other's enjoyment without the usual defenses: the subject agrees to be 'played.' The right-hand version is a trusting relation to that Other. The left-hand version, in which the Shadow is trained and then released, is the subject trying to be the master of the Other's enjoyment, which Lacan would see as the structure of perversion. This is an interpretive layer added for this app.

Joseph Dartez, The Tarot According to Ra (Draft 1), Relationship #12, pp. 161-164
Joseph Dartez, The Tarot According to Ra (Draft 1), Ra, 49.6 (the phrase "the crown is already upon the head" and "sacramental"), as cited by Dartez

22.name: The Fool
22.framework: The Choice is the unifying archetype expressing the holistic nature of the entire third density experience. It is both beginning and end—the spiritual neophyte stepping into mystery and the one exiting third density firmly committed to their path. Ra calls it 'relatively fixed and single' compared to other archetypes. The Choice represents the locus of 'free will, in the full sense'—the self that chooses between the two moral paths.
22.character: Dartez calls the persona the Traveler, who is neither masculine nor feminine (he arbitrarily uses 'she'). She is the audience who experiences life through the protagonist's eyes, so she is related to Campbell's Hero but exists outside the story. The archetype has two meanings: the beginning, where she steps blindfolded into a world she knows nothing about, and the end, where third density is complete and she walks, with the choice made, into the next density. At the start she is driven by curiosity, faith that it will work out, and ignorance of the danger; no one has beaten the path she walks, so she makes it. Dartez links the blindfold to the veiling and suggests the parable of the Prodigal Son for the decision to leave the unity of the Creator. Commentators call this card the Atheist or Materialist because she can only see the illusion's materiality. The central lesson is that we live and die as fools: we will not know the truth of the illusion except in our hearts, and will never feel enlightened. (He cites Carla Rueckert saying we are all Bozos on this bus.) Her function is to witness the drama of the evolution of mind, body and spirit: at each stop she identifies with some characters and not others, decides whether the drama suits her, and decides when to move on. Her motive is curiosity and spiritual longing, her empowering capacities are faith and naivety, her virtue is humility (in a later passage he lists the Fool's virtues as humility, faith and bold naivety).
symbols: Blindfolded figure walking toward the ocean - the ocean is the unknown, the blindfold is the veiling and the inability to see through the illusion, so any discovery has to rest on faith and feeling, not knowledge

Open-mouthed crocodile - the dangers of the path: not just loss of life or limb but mental and spiritual disfigurement; we can end up in a more confused spiritual state than we began, or even achieve the opposite of what we planned before incarnating
Fallen column with writing - the mainstream social structures and the popular idea of a good life; fallen because they failed to satisfy the figure's spirit
Solar eclipse - echoes the darkness of the blindfold, and the choice between the two moral paths; on the ending side of the card, the choice the Fool has firmly made
Two bags on the left shoulder, one in front and one behind - her few possessions, some known and some hidden: contracts for experience with other souls and a set of non-negotiable core values
Black walking stick in the right hand, behind her - the ability to stay upright on the road, somewhat hindered because the stick is behind her
Half-nakedness - vulnerability to the path's dangers

levels.personal: The subjective witness present to every moment: the eye that does not see itself. It usually identifies with whatever part of the psyche is active, and now and then steps back to ask whether it wants to go on as before.
levels.interpersonal: The Traveler who joins others in their home, mental, physical or spiritual. A welcome guest because she adapts, a chameleon both familiar and mysterious who listens more than she speaks and respects the traditions of the house. She can take on any other persona, so Dartez calls her the persona of personality. Her choice is whether to stay or pack up and go.
levels.social: The immigrant, the well-traveled newcomer, whose experience is wider than the culture she has entered, and who understands a new place easily but finds it hard to put down roots and feels like an outsider in someone else's community.

polarizedExpressions.note: Dartez concludes that the Choice admits distorted modes of expression but not dual polarized virtuous ones. Ra calls it 'relatively fixed and single,' which he reads as a matter of how we know it, and not of how it is expressed. The Fool is the chooser, not the thing chosen: the self she chooses for or against is the Significator, and the objective archetypes are the ones that split into right- and left-hand forms.

distortions: Arrogance and rashness - quick to judge that she understands a situation she does not; the virtue is boldly entering a new world, the vice is believing she already understands it, which invites retaliation from the strange world (the crocodile)

Faithlessness - she is energized to leave the beaten path but too afraid of the unknown to go on; the virtuous Fool is not courageous (courage means acting despite fear) but fearless because she has faith that what she finds will be nourishing and beautiful

Cynicism - derived from faithlessness and arrogance; the traditional Atheist or Materialist; Dartez argues that claiming there is no God or nothing but matter is empirically unfounded and that the honest position is agnosticism

raQuotes.text: The last concept complex may best be termed the Choice.
The polarization, or choosing, of each mind/body/spirit is necessary for harvestability from third density. The higher densities do their work due to the polarity gained in this choice.

A proper understanding, if we may use this misnomer, of archetype twenty-two is greatly helpful in sharpening the basic view of the Significator of Mind, Body, and Spirit; and, further, throws into starker relief the transformation and great way of mind, body, and spirit complexes.

22.jungian: The Fool represents the archetype of the Eternal Youth (puer aeternus) and the Wise Old Man simultaneously—beginner's mind that is also complete wisdom. The Traveler is the Self before and after differentiation: the same consciousness that enters incarnation and exits it, unchanged by the journey yet enriched by experience. The blindfold marks the necessary not-knowing that protects free will: if we saw clearly, we could not choose authentically. The crocodile (shadow danger) and fallen column (collective failure) frame the individual's passage. The Fool is who we are beneath all roles: witness to our own drama, capable of departing any scene when it no longer serves.
22.lacanian: The Fool figures the subject of the unconscious—the dimension of subjectivity that is not the ego, not the self-image, but the gap or discontinuity that makes self-consciousness possible. The Traveler is the barred subject ($): divided, lacking, yet capable of desire precisely because of this division. The blindfold represents structural not-knowing: the subject cannot see themselves seeing, cannot know the desire that motivates their knowing. The two bags are the objet a (behind, unknown) and the ego-ideal (in front, known): what actually causes desire versus what we believe causes it. The Fool's 'relatively fixed' nature reveals the subject as purely formal: not a substance but a position, the same empty place through which all content passes.
sources: Joseph Dartez, The Tarot According to Ra (Draft 1), pp. 40-44
